attribution.note: Marcus states the consensus claim in his own voice.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the retrospective claim of near-universal agreement, including the CEOs.

contract.note: Automatically failing on one major dissenter strengthens near-universal agreement into unanimity. The contract also inconsistently permits non-opposition while treating omission as contradiction. Rejecting global governance does not itself reject international dialogue or cooperation.

evidence.note: Amodei endorses testing, external evaluation, international cooperation and urgent work. This supports several components, but does not establish agreement on liability.
Altman endorses risk assessment, verification and international cooperation. The excerpt does not establish endorsement of liability; omission alone does not establish opposition.
Bengio explicitly supports the listed measures, including liability. The reported keyword search cannot establish every speaker's substantive position or the extent of consensus.
The US rejects global governance but expressly endorses international dialogue, cooperation and testing. This does not demonstrate rejection of Marcus's listed cooperation measure.

reviews.rationale: The excerpts establish substantial agreement on several measures, but do not establish nearly all speakers' agreement on all five. Liability endorsement remains inadequately documented. The proposed contradiction relies on an unfair unanimity rule and conflates opposition to global governance with opposition to cooperation.

attribution.note: Marcus himself makes the criticism; its attribution does not depend on the accompanying Rasmussen quotation.

semantics.note: The normalization closely preserves the wording and qualifications. The surrounding passage places the criticism in the context of Amodei's UN speech.

contract.note: The contract expands a criticism of the speech to a separate announcement post and treats suggesting gene editing as a CRISPR comparison. It also assumes that comparison before functional validation establishes overhyping, without accounting for explicit preliminary qualifications.

evidence.note: The speech suggests possible gene-editing applications with explicit preliminary qualifications. It does not name CRISPR or independently establish the alleged comparison.
Reports a same-day CRISPR comparison by Amodei in his announcement post. This supports that narrower fact, but does not locate the comparison in the speech.
Reports the preprint's admission that enzyme activity and function remained unshown. This supports the discovery's preliminary status, but does not alone establish overhyping.
An identified researcher criticizes presenting the preliminary findings as a major discovery. This supports Marcus's assessment, but does not establish precisely what Amodei compared in the speech.
The report recognizes genuine similarities to CRISPR, scientific interest and no false assertion. These qualify the criticism, although factual accuracy does not exclude exaggeration.

reviews.rationale: The packet supports a same-day comparison in an announcement post and the absence of demonstrated enzyme function. It does not establish the alleged CRISPR comparison in the speech. The speech's qualifications and the reported genuine similarities also prevent those facts alone from settling whether Amodei overhyped the discovery.
